That rival has real force, especially from the language of reckoning, justification, forgiveness, and righteousness “without works.” Nevertheless, the book better integrates the supplied evidence. Deuteronomy 6:25, Psalm 119:172, and 1 John 3:7 directly connect righteousness with doing God’s commands, while Revelation 19:8 expressly identifies the garment as the saints’ righteous acts. The apparent Pauline counterevidence is answered coherently by distinctions already established in the prior findings: living faith includes obedient submission, works are deeds rather than a synonym for obedience, and Romans 4 targets work advanced as a wage claim that would place God in debt. Luke 17:7-10 independently confirms that even complete obedience remains duty rather than meritorious wage-work. Thus grace explains the source and reckoning of righteousness without changing wrongdoing into right-living.
